findings.original: In this process the labour-power is itself consumed by the capitalist while the means of production are consumed by the labour-power
findings.rewrite: In this process the capitalist himself consumes the labor-power, while the labor-power consumes the means of production
findings.problem: Marx's "itself" stresses that the labor-power, the consumer of the means of production, is in turn consumed; moving the emphasis to "the capitalist himself" changes the point of the sentence.
findings.fix: In this process the labor-power is itself consumed by the capitalist, while the means of production are consumed by the labor-power as it performs its function, labor.

findings.original: an analysis which, even from the bourgeois standpoint of the science, cries out for rectification
findings.rewrite: although even from the bourgeois standpoint of the science it cries out to be corrected
findings.problem: The footnote 17 relative clause is turned into an "although" clause, adding a concessive link the original does not make.
findings.fix: an analysis that, even from the bourgeois standpoint of the science, cries out to be corrected.

notes_review: The logged calls are sound: the literal retranslation of the Necker brackets, matching Storch's "résoudre" and Marx's mocking repetition with the same verb, keeping "productive labour"/"productive labourer" as mentioned terms, and leaving "his master's" unnamed all respect fidelity.
summary: Fidelity is high: Ricardo's and Smith's quoted words, the echoed "There can be no greater error", and the separation of Smith's cloth-manufacturer example from Marx's comment are all intact; two small shifts were found in p043 and its footnote. Readability is good.
